query: What sample sizes/power calculations are required to detect d=0.3 in mixed-effects models and to estimate a CFA with X factors and Y items?

response.query: What sample sizes/power calculations are required to detect d=0.3 in mixed-effects models and to estimate a CFA with X factors and Y items?
response.answer: To detect d=0.3 in mixed-effects models, a sample size of at least 200 is typically needed. For estimating a CFA with X factors and Y items, a minimum of 200-400 participants is generally recommended.

results.title: The case for the $3 million super tax - Firstlinks
results.content: They have paid tax all the way along – on contribution of funds to Super, on annual Income and on annual Capital Gains in Super, and they will pay an existing TAX ON DEATH of 17% on their Super balance. If you repealed the costello super pension taxation changes (where pension payments became tax free) and put back in place the regime where you were taxed on your super withdrawals, but had a 15% tax offset (to refund for the contributions and earnings tax you already paid) then there would be no need for this additional tax on high balances, and no need for the pension transfer limit (~$2m). So maybe the change that is required is that the 15% earnings tax continues to be applied to super funds in pension phase, but with the rebate of 15% on the pension actually paid (I know it sounds a bit like taking with one hand and giving back with the other, but it would only affect those with high super balances, which as Jon points out, were from after tax contributions).
